data.name: Sadhana
data.gender_notes: Sadhana is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root sādh, 'to accomplish' — sādhanā, 'practice, discipline'. Its root is Sanskrit sādh (साध्). A central concept in Hindu spiritual practice. Sadhana is a Sanskrit name meaning “Practice; spiritual discipline; fulfilment”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sadhana expresses “Practice; spiritual discipline; fulfilment”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root sādh, 'to accomplish' — sādhanā, 'practice, discipline'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadhana total 21, reducing to 3. Number 3 is associated with expression, creativity and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'सद्धन' (sadhana), which means 'truth' or 'wealth'. In Hinduism, Sadhana refers to the spiritual practices or disciplines undertaken to attain self-realization or union with the divine.
